one_month_reasoning: No Adobe-scheduled catalyst falls in 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30: Q3 FY26 was reported Sep 10, the Q4 FY26 print and first FY27 guide are expected ~Dec 9, Adobe MAX is Nov 10-12 and the CEO handover is Dec 1. Wadhwani's exit (effective Sep 27) is already public and priced (8-K filed Sep 8). Inside the window: late-October software/mega-cap earnings (AI-disruption sentiment factor) and the Oct 28 FOMC, where hike odds fell to ~35-37% after the soft Aug PCE on Sep 30. I drop my round-1 slight negative tilt (post-guide drift has had three weeks to play out) and use a near-symmetric lognormal centred ~$237.5 with monthly sigma ~11.5% (41% annual / 3.5), tails a touch fatter for the rate event.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$29.0 x 9.0x = $261, weight 0.6) and FCF-after-SBC yield (~$24.6/share on ~365M shares at a 9.25% yield, less ~$1.9/share net debt = ~$264, weight 0.4); fair value ~$262 at Sep 2027.

bear.story: The December FY27 guide, the first under a new CEO with an interim CFO and no core Creative president, resets expectations: organic net new ARR keeps falling (Q3 -36-37% y/y), freemium does not convert, and AI compute and marketing costs squeeze margins. Organic growth slides to mid-single digits and EPS of ~$26-27 gets 6.5-7x, as the market prices ADBE as a melting ice cube.

base.story: Q4 net new ARR comes in near the guide-implied ~-16% y/y, FY27 guide is roughly in line with organic ARR ~8%, and EPS grows ~10-12% with ~7% annual share shrink. The multiple holds ~8.5-9x NTM, so the upside comes from earnings and buybacks, not re-rating.

bull.story: AI-first ARR (+150%) and 1B MAU/freemium start converting, organic net new ARR stabilises in H1 FY27, and new management credibly defends ~45% margins. The multiple recovers to ~11-11.5x NTM EPS of ~$29.5.

thesis_break_reason: Below the $190 52-week low and ~6.3x NTM consensus EPS (~$29.6). With A+/A2 credit, net debt ~$0.7B, ~9% FCF yield after SBC and a buyback shrinking the count ~7%/yr, a trade there would most likely mean the Dec ~9 FY27 guide (new CEO, interim CFO, core Creative president gone) implies flat-to-declining organic net new ARR for another year or a structural margin reset, i.e. AI substitution showing up in the numbers rather than ordinary volatility. I keep $185 rather than the supervisor's $178 because my bear scenario centres at $180, so a close below $185 already means that story is playing out.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. Supervisor corrections, verified against primary sources: (1) my 'net new ARR ex-Semrush -3% y/y' was MBI's Q2 figure. On the Q3 call Evercore stated net new ARR was down 36-37% y/y, management did not dispute it (transcript checked), and since Semrush was already in the Q2 ARR it is essentially organic, so the bear fact is worse than I had it. The FY 10.2% ARR guide still implies Q4 net new ARR of ~-16% y/y, which is less bad. (2) The 8-K confirms Wadhwani, President of Creativity & Productivity, resigned effective Sep 27, which adds to December-guide execution risk. (3) I double-counted skepticism with a sub-consensus FY28 EPS and a 9x multiple. I now use consensus NTM at the correct fiscal weighting (~$29.6), with only a ~2% reset trim, at 9.0x, about today's multiple. (4) Share count: 389.2M now, ~7M net retired per quarter, so I use ~365M at Sep 2027 (slightly conservative vs ~362M). (5) FCF after SBC on TTM CFO of $10.81B gives ~$24.6/share at 9.25% = ~$264. Fair value moves from $256 to ~$262. The stronger organic-slowdown and leadership evidence roughly offsets the removal of the double haircut, so I raised the fair value only modestly and moved probability into the bear case (25% to 27%). What bears still lack: no accounting red flags, A+/A2 credit, immaterial net debt, and a ~9% after-SBC FCF yield funding ~$9B/yr of buybacks. The downside is a December reset story, not a solvency story. The mixture (bear $180/27%, base $256/48%, bull $335/25%; lognormal dispersion ~19-27%) gives a median ~$254, P(>=spot) ~57%, with tails slightly fattened for 41% realized volatility. Research was limited to 3 verification fetches (8-K, Q3 release, transcript). The supervisor's FY28 EPS of ~$30.0 comes from one aggregator, so I trimmed it.
